summary.intent: Implement SDK-based E2E and load test suites for CipherBox as two new workspace packages (tests/sdk-e2e and tests/load), replacing browser-automation Playwright tests with direct SDK calls for reliability and speed.
summary.outcome: Both packages fully implemented with 83 passing E2E tests across 10 suites, 5 load test scenarios with metrics infrastructure, throttle bypass mechanism, CI workflows, and all 26 PR review comments resolved across two review rounds.

repo: setApiClientConfig in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts is a module-level singleton used by orval-generated functions — all SDK operations share one global axios config, causing cross-contamination in multi-account tests

ThrottlerGuard is applied per-controller (not globally via APP_GUARD), imported from @nestjs/throttler — replacing with a custom guard requires updating all controller imports and all spec files that use .overrideGuard(ThrottlerGuard)
The IPNS publish endpoint has a strict per-endpoint @Throttle({ default: { limit: 10, ttl: 60000 } }) decorator (10 publishes/min) that is the primary bottleneck for SDK-heavy load tests
The API .env file takes precedence over shell environment variables for NestJS ConfigModule — setting NODE_ENV=test in the shell does not override .env when running via pnpm dev
POST /auth/test-login returns { accessToken, refreshToken, isNewUser, publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex } — the test login bypass already exists and uses TEST_LOGIN_SECRET
crypto.getRandomValues() has a 65,536 byte limit per call — generating load test files larger than 64KB requires chunked generation

The existing integration test at packages/sdk/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts lines 24-59 is the authoritative pattern for SDK test setup: test-login → initializeVault → encryptVaultKeys → setApiClientConfig → CipherBoxClient → registerFolder
CipherBoxClient exposes getFolderTree() as a public method — (client as any).folderTree casts in tests were unnecessary

code.finding: Added optional defaultHeaders to ApiClientConfig and wired it into the axios instance — allows test harnesses to inject bypass headers without per-call manual injection
New BypassableThrottlerGuard extends ThrottlerGuard, checks X-Throttle-Bypass header against THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET using Node.js crypto.timingSafeEqual, and includes NODE_ENV !== 'production' guard
ThrottlerModule configured with 10 req/s (ttl 1000ms) and 100 req/min (ttl 60000ms) limits — no global APP_GUARD, throttling is per-controller
setApiClientConfig must be re-called before tests that depend on it when running after multi-account test suites that overwrite the singleton
Generates random Uint8Array in 65536-byte chunks to work around crypto.getRandomValues limit
Exports testFetch() helper that injects X-Throttle-Bypass and Authorization headers for raw fetch calls in test suites that cannot use the generated API client

workflow: When replacing a guard class with a custom subclass, all spec files using .overrideGuard(OriginalClass) must be updated to target the new class — NestJS DI fails with dependency resolution errors otherwise

For load tests targeting environments with rate limiting, a secret-header bypass is preferable to loosening limits — but per-endpoint @Throttle decorators require the same guard class swap and staging secrets injected into CI
pnpm --filter <pkg> dev (NestJS watch mode) hot-reloads TypeScript changes but reads .env on startup — changes to .env require a full restart

orval-generated API client functions are standalone imports that call the singleton axios instance — instance-scoping would require orval config changes to pass an axios instance parameter through all generated functions

Running vitest with fileParallelism: false (sequential suites) does not prevent setApiClientConfig singleton contamination between suites — later suites see whatever token the previous multi-account suite left behind

friction: 1Password SSH agent times out in agent subprocesses — commits from Bash tool calls frequently hang on signing, requiring manual retry or user intervention from terminal
sed replace_all via Edit tool left dangling closing parentheses when replacing 'headers: {' with 'headers: fetchHeaders({' — caused TypeScript parse errors requiring full file rewrites

The throttle bypass only covers controllers using @UseGuards(BypassableThrottlerGuard) — per-endpoint @Throttle decorators on the IPNS publish endpoint still caused 429s in load tests even after implementing the bypass
NODE_ENV=test set in shell is silently overridden by NODE_ENV=development in .env — not obvious from NestJS docs which source wins
API unit test failures (Nest can't resolve THROTTLER:MODULE_OPTIONS) only surfaced in CI, not during local development — required a second review round to discover
open_items: Refactor api-client from module-level singleton to instance-scoped axios (tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-refactor-api-client-from-singleton-to-instance-scoped-axios.md) — this would eliminate testFetch, fetchHeaders, the setApiClientConfig re-set in error-cases, defaultHeaders, and multi-account switchTo hacks

Investigate @Throttle decorator bypass gap for IPNS publish endpoint (tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-investigate-throttle-bypass-gap-for-per-endpoint-throttle-decorators.md) — determine if 429s come from the throttler or upstream IPFS, verify bypass header propagation to IPNS requests
Load test scenarios for sustained-load and spike-test were written but not validated against the local stack — only upload-throughput, ipns-publish-storm, and mixed-workload were run

Test suites that use raw fetch (vault-lifecycle, share-operations, invite-link) should be migrated to use the generated API client once the singleton refactor lands — currently require testFetch() workaround
Load test workflow (load-test.yml) targets staging via workflow_dispatch but STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET GitHub secret needs to be created before the workflow can be used against staging
